text:
sarah-sales: Quick heads up — Lantern is asking for a POC to replace their existing API adapter and validate parity. They want: prompt/response parity, pricing comparison, and answers for their security questionnaire. They want a kickoff next Tue if possible.

tom-eng: Do we have a checklist of API surface gaps? specifically: streaming vs chunked, rate-limit headers, request IDs, and model variant names.

anjali-ps: We can do a focused 3-day POC: day1 = parity tests, day2 = load + latency, day3 = follow-ups + legal. Need a seed prompt set from Lantern and an expected-output tie-breaker policy.

matt-security: Lantern will need SOC2 evidence, encryption-at-rest details (KMS/HSM), VPC peering options, and data residency controls. Also confirm we can toggle logging redaction for their PII fields.

jess-devex: I've got a starter harness that maps Lantern's calls to Redwood. Example curl mapping to our chat endpoint:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-xl","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"${PROMPT}"}],"stream":false}'
```

We also have a small shim to translate their `client_request_id` header to our `x-request-id`. I'll drop the repo link in the thread.

tom-eng: Two engineering notes: 1) Tokenization differences — Lantern's models use a different tokenizer which causes mild token-count deltas (affects billing). We'll need to normalize or show cost delta on the same tokenization baseline. 2) Determinism: seeding behavior differs; results may not be bitwise identical. We'll define output-equivalence metrics.

sarah-sales: On pricing — they're pushing for per-token parity + a 15% committed volume discount in year1. Also asking if we support reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated. Can we get a quick estimate for their 50M monthly tokens?

matt-security: Also: retention windows and deletion APIs. They require a DPA + ability to delete logs on request. Legal should prep a DPA draft; I'll own the SSO/KMS answers.

anjali-ps: Proposed acceptance criteria for the POC (suggestions):
- Functional parity: >95% semantic-match on 10k prompt seed set using our fuzzy-match and human spot-check.
- Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 400ms for their typical 64-token responses under baseline load.
- Cost delta: total token cost delta < 10% after normalizing tokenization.
- Security: SOC2 evidence + DPA + VPC tunnel test.

infra-bot: infra-bot: POC env requested. Dedicated trial pool (2 x A10G) will be provisioned in staging-redwood-us-west-2. Env ready ETA: 48h.

tom-eng: For routing/fallback we should propose an A/B mapping and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency SLO misses. Example route snippet: 

```yaml
routes:
  - name: lantern-poc
    match: { header: { 'x-customer': 'lantern' } }
    primary: redwood-1-xl
    fallback: redwood-1-medium
    latency_slo_ms: 250
```

jess-devex: I'll prepare the test harness config and a short runbook: how to normalize inputs (strip vendor-system prefixes), how we seed randomness for reproducibility, and the eval script for semantic-match scoring.

sarah-sales: Action items: 1) schedule kickoff for Tue 10am PT (I'll send calendar invite), 2) ask Lantern to share seed prompt set + security questionnaire, 3) engineering to estimate cost for 50M tokens and reserved capacity options, 4) security to start DPA + SOC2 packaging.

matt-security: I'll reach out to Lantern's compliance contact and request their questionnaire now. Also will collect the SOC2 checklist we can share.

anjali-ps: I'm available to run the parity suite Wed-Thu once infra is ready. I'll own the POC report and the acceptance matrix.

sarah-sales: Perfect — I'll cc legal and send the invite. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
